name: Unity
description: Commercial cross-platform engine with C# scripting and IL2CPP ahead-of-time compilation to C++ for native platforms. Official Android export produces Gradle projects and arm64-v8a libraries.
requirements: Unity Editor with Android Build Support module
Android SDK and NDK installed through Unity Hub
IL2CPP scripting backend for arm64-v8a
Gradle 8.x and JDK 17 for current Unity 6 Android builds
limitations: Editor and Android build modules are not available inside Termux
IL2CPP output is generated C++; hand-porting the engine itself is not the supported path
Asset bundles are version-locked to the engine build that produced them

name: Unreal Engine
description: C++ engine with Blueprint visual scripting and a source-available license. Android support ships as part of the engine with Vulkan and OpenGL ES rendering paths and a dedicated packaging pipeline.
requirements: Epic Games account and engine source access
Android Studio with NDK r25b or the version pinned by the engine release
Project packaged as ASTC or ETC2 textures for mobile
Vulkan-capable device for the Vulkan RHI path
limitations: Full source build is tens of gigabytes and impractical on a phone
Cooked content is platform-specific and must be re-cooked for Android
Android packaging officially expects a desktop host with the full SDK/NDK

license.name: Unreal Engine End User License Agreement

name: Godot Engine
description: MIT-licensed engine with GDScript and C++ (GDExtension) scripting. Android export templates are official and support Vulkan (Forward+) and OpenGL ES 3 (Compatibility) renderers.
requirements: Godot editor plus matching export templates
Android SDK and NDK for custom builds
JDK 17 for Gradle export
limitations: Export templates must match the editor version exactly
Vulkan renderer needs a Vulkan 1.0+ device; the Compatibility renderer is the safe fallback
PCK assets are engine-version dependent

name: GameMaker
description: 2D-focused commercial engine using GameMaker Language and YoYo Compiler output. Android export is an official target that packages a runner with compiled game data.
requirements: GameMaker subscription that includes Android export
Android SDK/NDK configured in the GameMaker preferences
data.win game data produced by the compiler
limitations: Linux IDE support is limited compared to Windows/macOS
Runtime source is closed; porting means using the official export or reimplementing the runtime
GML is not portable to other engines without a rewrite

name: Cocos2d-x
description: MIT-licensed C++ 2D engine with Lua and JavaScript bindings. Android projects are generated through CMake and the NDK, making it one of the few engines that can be built end-to-end with command-line tools.
requirements: NDK r21+ and CMake 3.10+
Python 2 or 3 for the project generator scripts
OpenGL ES 2.0/3.0 capable device
limitations: Project generator tooling is dated and needs patches on modern Python
Vulkan backend is not the default path
Community activity has slowed compared with Unity/Godot

name: Defold
description: Lightweight Lua-scripted engine with an official Android target. The editor is proprietary but the engine runtime source is available under the Defold License.
requirements: Defold editor
Android SDK/NDK configured in editor preferences
Bob.jar for command-line builds
limitations: Rendering is OpenGL ES based; no Vulkan renderer
Editor is closed source
Extension system requires re-bundling native code

name: Source 2
description: Valve's proprietary engine used by Counter-Strike 2 and Deadlock. No public SDK and no Android target; the engine ships only Windows/Linux builds for its own titles.
requirements: Valve developer access for any engine-level work
Windows or Linux x86-64 host
limitations: No public engine SDK
No ARM or Android build path
Asset formats are undocumented and versioned per title

name: Source (Source SDK 2013)
description: Valve's previous-generation engine with a public SDK for mods. x86 32-bit only, Direct3D 9 and OpenGL rendering, no official Android or ARM64 path.
requirements: Visual Studio 2013 or a patched modern toolchain
32-bit build target
limitations: 32-bit address space cap
No ARM64 or Android support
Tied to Steam APIs for retail titles

name: GoldSrc
description: Valve's Quake-derived engine used by Half-Life and its mods. Closed source, 32-bit x86, software and OpenGL rendering, no Android target.
requirements: Original game files for any content
32-bit x86 host
limitations: No source release
No ARM or Android support
Runs on Android only through emulation or community reimplementations

name: id Tech 3
description: Quake III Arena engine, released under GPL-2.0. C language, OpenGL fixed-function era rendering. Several community Android ports exist because the source is free.
requirements: GPL-2.0 compliance for any distributed build
Original game data (pak0.pk3) supplied by the user
OpenGL ES translation or a GLES renderer backport
limitations: Fixed-function GL assumptions need a GLES2+ renderer
Community Android ports vary in completeness
32-bit assumptions in the original code

name: id Tech 4 (Doom 3 BFG)
description: Doom 3 engine with the BFG Edition source release under GPL-2.0. C++ codebase with OpenGL rendering and a public Android port lineage.
requirements: GPL-2.0 compliance
User-supplied game data
GLES2/3 renderer backport or GL translation
limitations: Desktop GL renderer must be replaced or translated
Large asset set for mobile storage
Community ports differ in feature completeness

name: Ren'Py
description: Visual-novel engine written in Python with an official Android build path through the RAPT tooling. Games are script files plus assets packaged into an APK.
requirements: Ren'Py SDK matching the game version
RAPT (Ren'Py Android Packaging Tool)
JDK 17 for current Gradle versions
limitations: 2D only; no 3D pipeline
RAPT needs a desktop host with the Android SDK
Python-level game logic is tightly coupled to the Ren'Py runtime

name: LÖVE
description: Lua 2D framework with an official Android port. Games are a .love zip loaded by the runtime; the Android build embeds the game archive in the APK.
requirements: LÖVE Android build tooling and NDK
LuaJIT for arm64 (armeabi-v7a uses LuaJIT too)
Game packaged as .love
limitations: OpenGL ES 2/3 only
No built-in 3D renderer
LuaJIT and arm64 have a long-standing compatibility history that must be checked per build

name: libGDX
description: Java/Kotlin game framework where Android is a first-class backend. Desktop and Android share core game code; native code is optional through JNI.
requirements: JDK 17+ and Gradle
Android SDK with the target platform installed
gdx-backend-android dependency
limitations: JVM memory pressure on low-RAM devices
Desktop-only APIs need backend-specific code
Vulkan backend is experimental compared with the GLES backend

name: Bevy
description: Rust ECS game engine built on wgpu. Android support works through cargo tooling and the android-activity crate; it is usable but less turnkey than Unity or Godot.
requirements: Rust toolchain with the aarch64-linux-android target
cargo-ndk and Android SDK/NDK
Vulkan-capable device for the default wgpu backend
limitations: Android setup is manual compared with engine editors
No official editor or asset pipeline
wgpu on GLES is a fallback and feature-limited

name: MonoGame
description: Open-source C# reimplementation of the XNA 4 API. Android support comes through the .NET Android workload and produces a native APK with an assembly store.
requirements: .NET 8 SDK with the android workload
Android SDK and JDK 17
MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task for assets
limitations: Android workload installation is large and needs a desktop host
Content pipeline is XNA-era and can be brittle
No Vulkan backend in the mainline renderer

name: RPG Maker MV / MZ
description: Commercial 2D RPG engine whose runtime is JavaScript on NW.js. Android distribution is not an official export target and relies on third-party WebView or NW.js wrappers.
requirements: RPG Maker license for the editor
A WebView or NW.js Android wrapper supplied by a third party
Project deployed as www/ HTML+JS
limitations: No official Android exporter
Third-party wrappers vary in plugin compatibility
NW.js desktop APIs are unavailable in a plain WebView

name: OGRE
description: Object-oriented C++ 3D rendering engine with official CMake support and an Android sample build. Rendering only; game logic, physics and audio are supplied by the project.
requirements: CMake 3.20+ and NDK
Android sample or a custom Activity + JNI shell
OpenGL ES 3 device
limitations: No game framework: input, audio, physics must be integrated separately
Android support is sample-level, not a full editor export
Asset pipeline requires OGRE mesh conversion

name: Electron / NW.js web-tech games
description: Games built as HTML5/JavaScript bundles shipped inside a Chromium runtime. Android porting means re-hosting the web bundle in a WebView or a mobile browser rather than shipping Electron.
requirements: The original web bundle (HTML/JS/WASM)
A WebView host app with file access configured
WASM and WebGL2 support in the system WebView
limitations: Node.js and desktop Electron APIs are unavailable in a WebView
Native modules must be replaced or recompiled
Performance depends on the device WebView version

license.name: MIT License (Electron); game code license varies
